extracted.intended_audience: journal editors, publishers, and researchers (especially social and behavioral sciences)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines (the TOP guidelines) for journals to set author policies that promote transparency, openness, and reproducibility across publication practices via eight standards and a three-level implementation framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Extend article citation norms to data, code, and research materials so these contributions receive regular and rigorous citation credit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Level 0: Journal encourages citation of data, code, and materials—or says nothing. Level 1: Journal describes citation of data in guidelines to authors with clear rules and examples. Level 2: Article provides appropriate citation for data and materials used, consistent with journal's author guidelines. Level 3: Article is not published until appropriate citation for data and materials is provided that follows journal's author guidelines. Implementation notes: provide concrete citation formats/examples in author instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data transparency (data sharing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Incentivize or require authors to make underlying data available in trusted repositories to enable reproduction and reuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Level 0: Journal encourages data sharing—or says nothing. Level 1: Article states whether data are available and, if so, where to access them. Level 2: Data must be posted to a trusted repository; exceptions must be identified at article submission. Level 3: Data must be posted to a trusted repository, and reported analyses will be reproduced independently before publication. Examples of trusted repositories: Dataverse, Dryad, ICPSR, Open Science Framework, Qualitative Data Repository. Implementation notes: require repository link in article; allow documented exceptions for ethics/IP/resource constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytic methods (code) transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage or require sharing of code (scripts, analysis code, simulation code) used to generate reported results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Level 0: Journal encourages code sharing—or says nothing. Level 1: Article states whether code is available and, if so, where to access it. Level 2: Code must be posted to a trusted repository; exceptions must be identified at article submission. Level 3: Code must be posted to a trusted repository, and reported analyses will be reproduced independently before publication. Implementation notes: require working links; Level 2 includes editorial checks that links resolve; Level 3 may require editors or reviewers to re-run analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research materials transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Promote availability of research materials (questionnaires, stimuli, protocols, manuals, etc.) necessary to reproduce the methodology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Level 0: Journal encourages materials sharing—or says nothing. Level 1: Article states whether materials are available and, if so, where to access them. Level 2: Materials must be posted to a trusted repository; exceptions must be identified at article submission. Level 3: Materials must be posted to a trusted repository, and reported analyses will be reproduced independently before publication. Implementation notes: specify what counts as materials; require repository links and document exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design and analysis transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Increase transparency about research design and analysis plans to reduce vague or incomplete methodological reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Level 0: Journal encourages design and analysis transparency or says nothing. Level 1: Journal articulates design transparency standards. Level 2: Journal requires adherence to design transparency standards for review and publication. Level 3: Journal requires and enforces adherence to design transparency standards for review and publication. Implementation notes: standards can include detailed reporting checklists, templates, required disclosure of sampling, stopping rules, manipulations, measurement, and analysis choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preregistration of studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Record existence of studies in public registries to facilitate discovery of research (including unpublished studies) and reduce publication bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Level 0: Journal says nothing. Level 1: Journal encourages preregistration of studies and provides link in article to preregistration if it exists. Level 2: Journal encourages preregistration of studies and provides link in article and certification of meeting preregistration badge requirements. Level 3: Journal requires preregistration of studies and provides link and badge in article to meeting requirements. Implementation notes: use registries appropriate for discipline; badges/certificates can reward compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preregistration of analysis plans (preanalysis plans)
rubrics_metrics.description: Require or encourage registration of analysis plans so that confirmatory vs exploratory analyses are distinguishable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Level 0: Journal says nothing. Level 1: Journal encourages preanalysis plans and provides link in article to registered analysis plan if it exists. Level 2: Journal encourages preanalysis plans and provides link in article and certification of meeting registered analysis plan badge requirements. Level 3: Journal requires preregistration of studies with analysis plans and provides link and badge in article to meeting requirements. Implementation notes: clearly define what constitutes an acceptable analysis plan and how deviations will be reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replication standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize and facilitate publication of replication studies and define conditions under which replications will be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Level 0: Journal discourages submission of replication studies—or says nothing. Level 1: Journal encourages submission of replication studies. Level 2: Journal encourages submission of replication studies and conducts blind review of results. Level 3: Journal uses Registered Reports as a submission option for replication studies with peer review before observing the study outcomes. Implementation notes: provide submission pathways (e.g., Registered Reports), clarify review criteria for replications, and adopt practices to reduce bias against null results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Levels framework (0–3) for implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: A three-level modular scoring framework for each standard allowing journals to adopt minimal to stringent requirements (plus Level 0 for noncompliance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Level 0: no standard / encouragement only. Level 1: low barrier, minimal implementation (e.g., disclosure statements, links). Level 2: stronger author requirements (e.g., mandatory deposition in trusted repositories, editorial checks) without large resource burdens. Level 3: strongest enforcement (e.g., independent reproduction of analyses, required preregistration) which may require more editorial resources. Use the levels to choose feasible initial steps and to progress incrementally; publication badges and replication checks are examples of Level 2/3 actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions and accommodations (ethical, IP, resource constraints)
rubrics_metrics.description: Process for identifying and handling legitimate exceptions to sharing requirements due to ethical issues, intellectual property, or unavailable resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: Journals should specify acceptable exceptions at submission (e.g., sensitive human-subject data, proprietary materials), document them in the article, and provide alternatives (e.g., controlled-access repositories, redacted/shared metadata). Level 2 policies require that exceptions be identified at submission; Level 3 policies must still accommodate legitimate exceptions but should require justification and provide transparent statements in the publication about the exception. Implementation notes: develop review procedures for exception requests and consider data-use agreements or restricted-access repositories.
